c01.display: Welcome back to NLP, Simply Explained. This is unit 4, lesson 3: recurrent neural networks, or RNNs.
c01.spoken: Welcome back to N L P, Simply Explained. This is unit 4, lesson 3: recurrent neural networks, or R N ens.

c02.display: Word vectors give each word a meaning. But a sentence is more than a bag of words: order matters. Today we meet a network that reads in order.
c02.spoken: Word vectors give each word a meaning. But a sentence is more than a bag of words: order matters. Today we meet a network that reads in order.

c03.display: Here's the idea. A recurrent neural network reads one word at a time, and carries a memory forward from each word to the next.
c03.spoken: Here's the idea. A recurrent neural network reads one word at a time, and carries a memory forward from each word to the next.

c04.display: RNN stands for recurrent neural network. It reads a sequence step by step, and passes a hidden state, a kind of memory, from each step to the next.
c04.spoken: RNN stands for recurrent neural network. It reads a sequence step by step, and passes a hidden state, a kind of memory, from each step to the next.

c05.display: Reading "the cat sat", it updates its memory after the, again after cat, and again after sat.
c05.spoken: Reading "the cat sat", it updates its memory after the, again after cat, and again after sat.

c06.display: Think of reading a book while keeping a running summary in your head. Each new sentence updates the summary.
c06.spoken: Think of reading a book while keeping a running summary in your head. Each new sentence updates the summary.

c07.display: Here's what happens at every single word.
c07.spoken: Here's what happens at every single word.

c08.display: Read: take the vector for the next word.
c08.spoken: Read: take the vector for the next word.

c09.display: Combine: mix it with the memory carried over from the previous step.
c09.spoken: Combine: mix it with the memory carried over from the previous step.

c10.display: Update: that mix becomes the new memory.
c10.spoken: Update: that mix becomes the new memory.

c11.display: Output: if needed, use the memory to produce something, like a guess for the next word. Then move on, and do it all again.
c11.spoken: Output: if needed, use the memory to produce something, like a guess for the next word. Then move on, and do it all again.

c12.display: Why is this better than the n-gram language models from unit one?
c12.spoken: Why is this better than the n-gram language models from unit one?

c13.display: An n-gram model only looks back a fixed few words, and counts exact sequences, so it knows nothing about phrases it never saw.
c13.spoken: An n-gram model only looks back a fixed few words, and counts exact sequences, so it knows nothing about phrases it never saw.

c14.display: An RNN's memory can, in principle, hold the whole sentence so far. And because it works with word vectors, what it learns about rain also helps with storm.
c14.spoken: An RNN's memory can, in principle, hold the whole sentence so far. And because it works with word vectors, what it learns about rain also helps with storm.

c15.display: Before today's models arrived, RNNs powered much of NLP.
c15.spoken: Before today's models arrived, R N ens powered much of N L P.

c16.display: Language models, guessing the next word.
c16.spoken: Language models, guessing the next word.

c17.display: Tagging, giving every word a label, like a part of speech.
c17.spoken: Tagging, giving every word a label, like a part of speech.

c18.display: And translation: one RNN reads a sentence in one language, and another writes it out in a different language.
c18.spoken: And translation: one RNN reads a sentence in one language, and another writes it out in a different language.

c19.display: How does an RNN learn? With a method called backpropagation through time. Picture the network unrolled across all the words. We measure its error, then send that error backwards through every step, adjusting the weights a little.
c19.spoken: How does an RNN learn? With a method called backpropagation through time. Picture the network unrolled across all the words. We measure its error, then send that error backwards through every step, adjusting the weights a little.

c20.display: So a mistake at word ten can send blame all the way back to word one.
c20.spoken: So a mistake at word ten can send blame all the way back to word one.

c21.display: It's like replaying a chess game move by move, to find which early move really cost you the game.
c21.spoken: It's like replaying a chess game move by move, to find which early move really cost you the game.

c22.display: But there's a catch, known as the vanishing gradient problem. Take: "The keys that I left on the kitchen table yesterday are missing." To choose "are" rather than "is", the network must remember "keys" from far back.
c22.spoken: But there's a catch, known as the vanishing gradient problem. Take: "The keys that I left on the kitchen table yesterday are missing." To choose "are" rather than "is", the network must remember "keys" from far back.

c23.display: The trouble is that the learning signal fades a little at every step it travels back.
c23.spoken: The trouble is that the learning signal fades a little at every step it travels back.

c24.display: After many words, it has almost vanished.
c24.spoken: After many words, it has almost vanished.

c25.display: So plain RNNs struggle to remember the start of long sentences. Next lesson fixes this.
c25.spoken: So plain R N ens struggle to remember the start of long sentences. Next lesson fixes this.

c26.display: Quick quiz. What does an RNN pass from one word to the next?
c26.spoken: Quick quiz. What does an RNN pass from one word to the next?

c28.display: Its hidden state: a kind of memory that carries what it has read so far.
c28.spoken: Its hidden state: a kind of memory that carries what it has read so far.

c29.display: Let's recap. An RNN reads a sentence one word at a time.
c29.spoken: Let's recap. An RNN reads a sentence one word at a time.

c30.display: It carries a hidden state, its memory, from each word to the next.
c30.spoken: It carries a hidden state, its memory, from each word to the next.

c31.display: It learns by backpropagation through time.
c31.spoken: It learns by backpropagation through time.

c32.display: But plain RNNs tend to forget the start of long sentences.
c32.spoken: But plain R N ens tend to forget the start of long sentences.

c33.display: Next lesson: LSTMs. How can a network remember something from far back in a sentence?
c33.spoken: Next lesson: L S T ems. How can a network remember something from far back in a sentence?
